• Manage symptoms such as pain,
stiffness & swelling
• Improve joint mobility & soft

• Improve muscle strength

walking aids, knee brace, shoe
orthotics, etc. to facilitate
functions & mobility

• Chronic inflammatory autoimmune
• systemic disease
• Chronic – long term
• Inflammatory – joint
• inflammation, thickening of
synovium, leading to swelling,
pain, +/- redness & warmth in
• joints

mistakenly attacks the joints

multiple organ systems
• Damage cartilage, bones & joints
• loss of cartilage, and narrow
joint spacing loose, unstable
joints with deformity

Signs & symptoms – Joints
• Joint pain, tenderness,
swelling, redness or stiffness
> 6 weeks
• Morning stiffness for > 1 hour
• > ONE joint are affected
• Small joints are commonly
• affected – Hands, Wrists &
toes
• Symmetrical joint pain: on
both sides of the body
• Decrease joint range of
• motion (ROM)
• Joint deformity
Flare - a period of high disease
activity, last for days/months
** increases in inflammation &
other symptoms

Signs & symptoms – organs & body systems
• Whole body: fatigue, loss of
appetite & low-grade fever
• Lungs: chest pain, shortness of
breath (SOB), persistent cough -
• inflammation & scarring
• Heart: chest pain - inflammation of
• tissue around the heart
• Eyes: dryness, pain, redness
• Blood vessels: affect blood flow
• Skin: rheumatoid nodules – small
lumps under the skin over bony
• areas
• Nerve: numbness, tingling, pain,
• weakness
• Blood: anaemia, low RBC
• Bone: Osteoporosis
• Mouth: dryness and gum problems

Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS)
• Relative uncommon rheumatic
disease that affect the spine
• Prevalence:
• Global – 0.1-1.4%
[Dean et al, 2014]
[Dean et al, 2014]
• Hong Kong – 0.2-0.3%
[Zhu et al, 2008]
[Zhu et al, 2008]
• long-term condition related
to autoimmune disease
• Joints and ligaments of spine and
other areas of the body become
• inflamed
• e.g. sacroiliac joint, hips,
• shoulders
• May involve other organs such
as eyes, lungs, heart

text:
Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS)
Treatment:
• No cure for AS, treatment
• available to relieve the
symptoms and delay
• progression
• Medications to reduce pain &
• inflammation:
• NSAIDS
• DMARDs, Biologics
• Corticosteriods
• Exercises: reduce pain &
• stiffness
• Physiotherapy: improve posture,
• flexibility, joint mobility
• Surgery: for rare cases to repair
significantly damaged joints or
correct severe bends in spine

text:
Osteoporosis
• A systemic metabolic
• disease of bone that leads
to a reduction in bone
mineral density (BMD)
• Affected bones become
thinner, more likely to
break (fractures) that may
result in pain & other
complications, including
loss of independence
• “Silent disease” - most
people don’t know they
have osteoporosis until
they suffer a broken bone
from a minor fall or bump

• Bone remodeling - continuous
process throughout life to
maintaining bone strength and
repairing micro-damage
• Osteoporosis is the imbalance
between bone resorption
(breakdown) by osteoclasts and
bone formation (building)
by osteoblasts, leading to a net
bone loss
(Chang et al, 2019)

Pharmacological Management
Anti-resorptive agents:
• Bisphosphonates: Alendronate
• (Fosamax), Risedronate
(Actonel), Ibandronate (Boniva)
• Denosumab (Prolia injection)
• Hormonal Replacement Therapy
• (HRT) & Selective Estrogen
• Receptor Modulators (SERM)
(SERM)
• reduce bone resorption,
preserving BMD
• Anabolic agents:
• Teriparatide (PTH1-34) (Forteo
• injection): parathyroid hormone
• Abaloparatide: parathyroid
• hormone-related protein
(PTHrP) (Tymlos injection)
(PTHrP) (Tymlos
• stimulate bone formation,
• thereby increasing BMD

Prevention of Osteoporosis
• Bone healthy lifestyle at all stages of
life
• Start building strong bones in
• childhood for stronger bones at
older age
• Healthy & balanced diet
• Enough Calcium & Protein
• intake
• Enough Vitamin D
• sunlight exposure
• taking food rich in Vitamin D
• Maintain healthy body weight with
• BMI ≥ 19
• Keep active with regular weight-
bearing and muscle strengthening
• ex
• Avoid smoking & heavy drinking
• Early detection & treatment if
having risk factor(s)

text:
Osteoporosis
• A systemic metabolic
• disease of bone that leads
to a reduction in bone
mineral density (BMD)
• Affected bones become
thinner, more likely to
break (fractures) that may
result in pain & other
complications, including
loss of independence
• “Silent disease” - most
people don’t know they
have osteoporosis until
they suffer a broken bone
from a minor fall or bump

Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling
• Bone remodeling - continuous
process throughout life to
maintaining bone strength and
repairing micro-damage
• Osteoporosis is the imbalance
between bone resorption
(breakdown) by osteoclasts and
bone formation (building)
by osteoblasts, leading to a net
bone loss
(Chang et al, 2019)

Risk Factors
Non-modifiable risk factors:
• Loss of height ≥ 4cm
• Stoop or curved upper back

• Previous fracture from minor

deficiency in oestrogen
• Medications: e.g. corticosteroid,
DM, anti-depressants…
• Other diseases: e.g. RA, GI tract
problems, COPD, Chronic Kidney
Disease, Endocrine Disorders
like hyperthyroidism…

Compound fracture
a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks
near the site of broken bone. Usually caused
by a fragment of bone breaking through the
skin during injury.
With broken skin, risk of infection due to
bacteria & other contaminants entering
wound.
Early treatment focuses on preventing
infection The wound, tissues & bone must
be cleaned out in surgical procedures as
soon as possible.
Fractured bone would be stabilized with a
surgical procedure to allow wound healing.
